17.1.en: Arjuna: "What about people who skip the rules but still have faith? What kind of faith is that?"
17.1.hi: Arjun: "Jo rules skip karte hain par bharosa rakhte hain? Woh kaisa bharosa hai?"

17.2.en: Krishna: "Faith comes in three types, based on your nature: pure, passionate or dark."
17.2.hi: Krishna: "Bharosa teen tarah ka hota hai, tumhari nature ke hisaab se: shuddh, josh bhara ya andhera."

17.3.en: You are what you believe in. Your faith shapes who you become.
17.3.hi: Tum wahi ho jis pe tum bharosa karte ho. Tumhara vishwas tay karta hai tum kya bante ho.

17.4.en: Pure people worship the divine, passionate people chase power, dark-minded people worship ghosts and spirits.
17.4.hi: Shuddh log divine ko poojte hain, josh wale power ke peeche, andhere wale bhoot-pret ko poojte hain.

17.5.en: Some people do extreme self-punishment just to show off, driven by ego and desire.
17.5.hi: Kuch log sirf dikhane ke liye extreme tapasya karte hain, ego aur chahat se chal ke.

17.6.en: Hurting your own body isn't spiritual. It hurts the divine in you too. That's a toxic mindset.
17.6.hi: Apne body ko takleef dena spiritual nahi. Isse tumhare andar ka divine bhi hurt hota hai. Ye toxic mindset hai.

17.7.en: Even food comes in three types. So does worship, discipline and giving. Let's break it down.
17.7.hi: Khaana bhi teen tarah ka hota hai. Pooja, tapasya aur daan bhi. Chalo breakdown karte hain.

17.8.en: Pure food: fresh, nourishing, wholesome, satisfying. It boosts health, energy, focus and happiness.
17.8.hi: Shuddh khaana: taaza, poshak, healthy, santusht karne wala. Sehat, energy, focus aur khushi badhata hai.

17.9.en: Passionate food: too spicy, salty, sour or hot. Tastes intense, leaves you uncomfortable and unwell.
17.9.hi: Rajasi khaana: zyada teekha, namkeen, khatta ya garam. Swaad intense, baad mein takleef aur bimaari.

17.10.en: Dark food: stale, leftover, tasteless, rotten. Junk that drags you down.
17.10.hi: Tamasi khaana: baasi, bacha hua, bina swaad, sada hua. Junk jo tumhe neeche kheenchta hai.

17.11.en: Pure worship is done because it's right, without expecting anything back.
17.11.hi: Shuddh pooja isliye hoti hai kyunki sahi hai, bina kuch wapas chahe.

17.12.en: Worship done for rewards or to show off is the passionate kind.
17.12.hi: Reward ke liye ya dikhawe ke liye ki gayi pooja rajasi hai.

17.13.en: Worship with no faith, no care, no sincerity and no giving is the dark kind.
17.13.hi: Bina bharose, bina parwaah, bina sachchai aur bina daan ki pooja tamasi hai.

17.14.en: Discipline of the body: respecting teachers and elders, staying clean, honest, self-controlled and non-violent.
17.14.hi: Body ka tap: guru aur badon ki izzat, saaf rehna, imaandaari, self-control aur ahimsa.

17.15.en: Discipline of speech: saying what's true, kind and helpful, without hurting anyone.
17.15.hi: Vaani ka tap: jo sach, pyaara aur faydemand ho woh bolna, bina kisi ko hurt kiye.

17.16.en: Discipline of the mind: calm, kind, quiet, self-controlled and pure thoughts.
17.16.hi: Mann ka tap: shaant, dayalu, maun, self-controlled aur shuddh vichaar.

17.17.en: All three done with faith and no expectations? That's the purest discipline.
17.17.hi: Teeno bharose aur bina umeed ke kiye? Ye sabse shuddh tap hai.

17.18.en: Discipline done for likes, respect and praise is the passionate kind. It doesn't last.
17.18.hi: Likes, izzat aur taareef ke liye kiya tap rajasi hai. Ye tikta nahi.

17.19.en: Discipline that's self-torture or meant to harm others is the dark kind.
17.19.hi: Jo tap khud ko takleef dene ya dusron ko nuksaan ke liye ho, woh tamasi hai.

17.20.en: Giving because it's right, to someone who deserves it, at the right time, expecting nothing back. That's pure giving.
17.20.hi: Sahi samajh ke dena, sahi insaan ko, sahi time pe, bina kuch wapas chahe. Ye shuddh daan hai.

17.21.en: Giving to get something back, or giving reluctantly, is the passionate kind.
17.21.hi: Kuch wapas paane ke liye dena, ya bemann se dena, rajasi daan hai.

17.22.en: Giving at the wrong time, to the wrong person, with disrespect, is the dark kind.
17.22.hi: Galat time pe, galat insaan ko, bina izzat ke dena tamasi daan hai.

17.23.en: "Om Tat Sat": three sacred words that point to the ultimate truth.
17.23.hi: "Om Tat Sat": teen pavitra shabd jo param satya ki taraf ishaara karte hain.

17.24.en: That's why the wise begin every sacred act by saying "Om".
17.24.hi: Isliye gyaani har pavitra kaam "Om" bol ke shuru karte hain.

17.25.en: Seekers say "Tat" and act without wanting rewards. It means: this is for the divine, not me.
17.25.hi: Saadhak "Tat" bol ke bina reward chahe kaam karte hain. Matlab: ye divine ke liye hai, mere liye nahi.

17.26.en: "Sat" means truth and goodness. Any good deed is called Sat.
17.26.hi: "Sat" ka matlab sach aur achhai. Har achha kaam Sat kehlata hai.

17.27.en: Staying committed to worship, discipline and giving is Sat too. So is any work done for that purpose.
17.27.hi: Pooja, tap aur daan mein lage rehna bhi Sat hai. Us maksad se kiya har kaam bhi.

17.28.en: Anything done without faith, even if it looks spiritual, is empty. Faith is what makes it count.
17.28.hi: Bina bharose kiya kuch bhi, chahe spiritual dikhe, khaali hai. Bharosa hi use count karata hai.
